tara (marketing): quick ask — can eng/runtime run a focused sanity rerun for the ensemble benchmark we plan to cite in the webinar?
We need a tiny, well-documented artifact pack we can hand to comms: raw latency p50/p90/p99, sample payloads, seeds, and exact CLI/config used. Target: 200 samples per variant. Deadline: EOD Friday. cc @matt @sam

matt (eng-runtime): yep, can do. couple quick clarifying qs: which model variants (sizes/quant)? and do you want warmup enabled?

tara (marketing): two variants: 1) 7B int8 (quantized) 2) 13B fp16 (baseline). For warmup: run both with warmup=0 and warmup=20 tokens (so we can show cold vs warmed). Also include one run with prefix-caching on for 13B.

sam (eng-ml): ordering: we'll run (a) 7B-int8 cold, (b) 7B-int8 warmup20, (c) 13B-fp16 cold, (d) 13B-fp16 warmup20, (e) 13B-fp16 warmup20+prefix-cache. Each 200 samples. I'll pin deterministic seeds.

matt (eng-runtime): plan: small fleet on staging-gpu-e cluster, batch config = auto-small, kv-cache toggles via --cache-prefix true/false. Will capture per-request trace, token counts, and raw server-side timestamps. Will dump a manifest tarball with: samples.jsonl, seeds.txt, run-config.json, raw-traces/ (gz). ETA: Friday 2pm PST.

tara (marketing): amazing — can you also include a short README with instructions on how you reproduced the run? simple steps for non-technical stakeholders.

matt (eng-runtime): yes. will include reproduction snippet and the exact CLI we used. example snippet below:

```
# example run command (simplified)
redwood-run --model gpt-7b-int8 --variant quantized --samples 200 --seed-file seeds.txt --warmup 20 --batching auto-small --output /tmp/ensemble-7b-int8-warmup20
```

sam (eng-ml): note: for fairness we use the same prompt set across variants. I'll attach the prompt header and a small 8-line seed manifest to keep v small in the artifact we share publicly. Also will redact any PII.

runtime-ci-bot: job created: job-2026-4555-01, queued on staging-gpu-e. Notifies on completion.

matt (eng-runtime): quick heads up: quantized runs have higher percentile variance on cold starts. I'll include a short notes.txt with caveats and recommended talking points (e.g., show warmed numbers as the primary metric, include coldstart callout).

tara (marketing): perfect — that commentary is helpful. If you can put recommended one-line copy for the webinar slide + one-sentence for the press pack that'd be great.

matt (eng-runtime): will do. tagging final ETA: Friday 2pm PST with artifact link and README. :thumbsup:

tara (marketing): thanks all — will prep slide placeholders and mark them as "pending artifacts". cheers!
